components.gap: Most definitions, theorems and lemmas of the chapter are reconstructed with written proofs, but parts of the source's own definitions and argument are missing. (1) Def. 9 (p. 270) asserts that ordinal equivalence holds iff T' = f(T) for some isotonic f; rationality-4-3.tex lines 291-293 state only that strictly increasing transforms preserve rankings, and the converse (ordinal equivalence yields one global isotonic f) is neither stated nor proved. (2) Def. 8(a) (p. 269) requires the value range of a relevance measure to be a subinterval, proper or improper, of the extended reals; lines 172-180 omit this clause. (3) The p. 268 motivation for the signpost notation, that for mutually relevant A and B, A may be more relevant to B than B is to A under one measure, less under another and equally under a third, is not presented or realized (lines 164-170; thm:p15-r43-measures shows only that D and L agree in direction and that Q is symmetric). (4) Linda (p. 273): the bridge of the argument, that E was designed to be representative of F and unrepresentative of B and that many probabilists explicate the representativeness of a property as the relevance of 'Linda is Phi' to E, is dropped; lines 485-489 reduce it to 'He treats that description as favoring feminist activity and disfavoring bank-teller work'. (5) Raven (p. 272): the source's statement of the problem (a plausible deductivist criterion requires the logical equivalents H and G to be supported alike, so B, and with mild further assumptions C, should support H, which is counterintuitive) and its claim that the negligible positive increment explains the pretheoretical intuition that B, and C, are irrelevant to H are not given (lines 398-425).

components.gap: (1) Linda (p. 273): the historical claim that the conjunction fallacy arose most famously in this late-1970s example, the empirical report that a surprisingly large proportion of respondents ranked BF above B (contravening P(BF|E) <= P(B|E)), and the design claim that E was built to be representative of F and unrepresentative of B are omitted; rationality-4-3.tex lines 479-509 give the task and the description but not the reported response pattern, so that empirical claim is not retained with its (unstated) population, design and uncertainty boundaries. (2) The claim-kind inventory def:p15-w02b-p15-024-claim-kinds (inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-024.tex lines 51-59) says the chapter contains three empirical claims; the chapter makes others, e.g. the Linda response proportion, the evidence that delta-p explicates participants' relevance assessments (p. 273), that relevance theory is popular in linguistics and conjectures relevance maximization as a principle of cognition and communication (p. 273), that D, Q and L are the oldest and most commonly used measures (p. 269), that LL is widely used in statistics (p. 270), and that many will balk at the symmetry of Q (p. 272). (3) Omitted normative or justificatory claims: p. 272 'Intuitions on amount symmetry are strong only in the case of asymmetric extreme positivity'; Q's symmetry in the 15/3 example 'which many will balk at, because it ignores the entailment asymmetry'; extreme valuation 'pleases anyone to whom conclusive argument is the strongest argument'; the homomorphism paragraph (structure-preserving maps essential to the predictability of ordinal and quantitative relevance properties of logical complexes; most conditional homomorphisms not practically useful, not all desirable); p. 273 conclusion 'one should seek out such independencies in one's domain of application'; p. 265 that the same relations obtain between statements about past events and between possible experimental results and timeless hypotheses, that 'speaking for' means being evidence for in the diction of jurisprudence and science, and that the informal idea remains vague and prone to apparent exceptions. (4) Note 15 ('(3) is an inessential embellishment that makes things vivid') is cited at line 425 but not presented, and the editorial note (Merin died on 24 May 2019; final minor revisions were made by the editors) is not recorded.

components.gap: The finite dependent-source set is fixed (33 references and 7 handbook chapters, def:p15-w02b-p15-024-dependents, inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-024.tex lines 947-1032) and every numbered theorem and lemma has written proofs, but not every promised proof or evidence claim is accounted for: (1) the Def. 9 equivalence of ordinal equivalence with isotonic transformation (p. 270) is given in one direction only (rationality-4-3.tex lines 291-293); (2) the p. 268 claim that the direction comparison for one pair can be greater under one measure, smaller under another and equal under a third is neither realized nor given a standing; (3) the chapter's empirical report on the Linda task (p. 273) and its attribution to many probabilists of the representativeness-as-relevance explication are not recorded, and the empirical-claim inventory (inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-024.tex lines 51-59) counts only three empirical claims, so these claims have no stated standing.
